title: Agent task report
description: Report every agent returns at the end of a task. All fields are required except verdict and overlapping_tool, which only the overlap role returns, and requester_message, which only the scoping role returns; a field that does not apply is null or an empty array. Cost and tokens are measured by the orchestrator, not declared here.

rule.description: Closed list, GENERATED by scripts/generate-report-catalogue.js from .claude/rules/*.md: every SEC-* entry of tests.md and every `<file>#<section>` heading. A value outside this list makes the report invalid (task failed, gap counted for the round). Never edit by hand.

category.description: Closed list, GENERATED by scripts/generate-report-catalogue.js: every `<file>#<section>` heading of .claude/rules/*.md plus `mechanical` and `data` (quality reviewer). Never edit by hand.

role.description: Role assigned by the orchestrator for this task.

task_id.description: Task identifier given by the orchestrator, copied verbatim.

status.description: done: the task is complete and verified. blocked: missing information, contradictory contract or a loop the agent cannot break; blocked_reason is mandatory. failed: the agent could not finish for a technical reason (tool error, budget, crash).

summary.description: One to three sentences a human can read without opening anything else.

verdict.description: Overlap role only, mandatory for it: plausible when a tool of the registry may already cover the need (say which one and why in summary), not_plausible when none does. Absent for every other role. The orchestrator reads this field, never the wording of summary; a missing or invalid verdict is treated as "to be checked" by the administrator (fail-closed).

overlapping_tool.description: Overlap role only, with verdict plausible: the slug of the catalogued tool that may cover the need, copied exactly from the catalogue given in the task. A plausible verdict naming a tool absent from that catalogue is treated as "to be checked" (fail-closed). Null or absent otherwise.

requester_message.description: Scoping role only: the message the requester reads with the mock-up link (questions with a recommended answer, then what is decided, assumed and still open), in business words only. The orchestrator refuses a message holding a technical word and sends the task back. Null or absent for every other role.

blocked_reason.description: Must be a non-empty string when status is blocked: the exact point that blocks (file, contract path, question). Null for any other status.

files_changed.description: Repository-relative paths of files created, modified or deleted. Empty for read-only roles.

verifications.description: Every verification command actually run, with its outcome. Never list a command that was not run.

command.description: The command as typed, e.g. `pnpm run verify`.

details.description: Short excerpt of the output that justifies the result (counts, failing test names). Empty string if nothing to add.

findings.description: Gaps found. For reviewers: one entry per instance, after the whole class of the gap has been searched. For code roles: gaps noticed outside your own folders that you could not fix. Empty when nothing was found.

id.description: Identifier unique within this report, e.g. F-001.

rule.description: Identifier of the rule or scenario violated: a SEC-* entry (e.g. SEC-IDOR) or `<file>#<section>` (e.g. backend.md#Errors), taken from the closed list ($defs.rule). The orchestrator identifies a gap across rounds by rule + file, never by text or line.

category.description: Category this finding belongs to, from the closed list ($defs.category); must match an entry of category_verdicts when the report has any.

file.description: Repository-relative path of the file concerned, or of the directory where the missing element belongs.

line.description: Line number in file, or null when the gap is an absence (missing test, missing header) rather than a line.

evidence.description: Concrete proof: the command run and its output, or a short excerpt. A code role's finding owned by tests gives the test line and the contract line, never code (the orchestrator withholds cited code before forwarding it). Never a supposition.

owner_role.description: Role that must fix it, deduced from the path: api/, db/, web/, tests/unit/ -> builder; tests/acceptance/ -> tests; openapi.yaml -> contract.

previous_id.description: Reviewers: the `id` of the finding in the previous review report of your role when this is the same problem, even if you now classify it under another rule or category. Null otherwise, and for every other role. Information for the orchestrator and the administrator: it can only link a gap to its predecessor, it never resets a stagnation counter.

category_verdicts.description: Reviewer roles only: one entry per category of the reference rule file, none skipped. Empty array for every other role.

category.description: Section heading of the reference rule file, e.g. `security.md#Requests`, or `mechanical` / `data` for the quality reviewer, from the closed list ($defs.category).

verdict.description: compliant only after an actual check. not_applicable and not_verified both require the reason in evidence.

evidence.description: What was checked and how (files read, commands run, tests found), or the reason for not_applicable / not_verified.

assumptions.description: Every choice made where the task, contract or rules left room. Empty if none.
